prerequisites: A general course on materials science during the previous Bachelor's degree
First semester courses of the Interuniversity Master's in Integrity and Durability of Materials, Components and Structures

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to analyze the ultimate causes of component failures that occurred during their service, to adopt appropriate corrective measures, and to prevent new failures.
Ability to assess the causes of structural failure, based on knowledge of the different failure processes.
Ability to handle the available tools for conducting failure analysis.
Ability to relate the results of the analysis to issue a final diagnosis of the failure.
Understand the processes originating in the material that lead to structural failures.
Understand the existing failure micromechanisms in different material families.
Understand the tools available for the practical execution of failure analysis.
Understand a wide variety of practical cases where the causes of failure of real structural components are determined.
Interpret the results obtained through different failure analysis tools.
Relate the different results obtained throughout a failure analysis.
Be able to diagnose the causes of a structural failure.
Foster in the student a desire for the acquisition of practical knowledge.
Advance the student's ability to apply acquired engineering knowledge.
Form an open, critical, cooperative, and entrepreneurial spirit.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Failure Analysis. Importance of in-service failures. Basic principles of failure analysis.
Fracture, Fatigue, Creep and CBT in Failure Analysis.
Failure Analysis Tools. Chemical and mechanical characterization. Microscopy techniques. Stress analysis and the finite element method. Defect detection systems. Structural Integrity procedures.
Practical cases. Resolution of real cases. Corrective and preventive measures. How to avoid future failures in these same facilities.
teaching_methods: External internships (in other institutions or companies)

assessment_methods.method: Individual report on the practical case(s) resolved throughout the course, potentially including small questionnaires related to it.
Group presentation of the work done in practical sessions.
Written test (multiple choice) on the complete course contents.

assessment_rules: A minimum of 4 points out of 10 is required for this final evaluation to pass the course.
